analysis:
Reviewed all four primary analyses against the supplied replayed patches, documentation and metadata. No independently supported security regression is established. The replay omits 10 source units, so surrounding controls described in prior analyses are not independently verified here.
.github/workflows/provider-release-cache.yml:76 selects qualification mode for PRs and release mode otherwise. provider-signing-validation.yml:57–60,136–139 replaces inline SDK 27.0 checks with reviewed toolchain preparation; lines 89–93 delegate native-build and SDK flags to the Swift wrapper. release-provider.yml:114 selects release mode globally, and :1444 changes the retained validation identity's exact SDK assertion to 27.2 while preserving adjacent source-commit and bundle-digest checks. docs/developer/build.md:162–188 and changelog.d/ci-xcode-27-2-toolchain.md:3–7 describe strict release selection and broader qualification selection, but are not evidence of enforcement.
These changes affect artifact integrity and qualification contracts (A-011, A-017, T-013, T-034, T-054). They do not visibly alter inference encryption, provider key custody, billing, local privilege boundaries or serving authorization. Under TB-011, release publication/toolchain validation remains distinct from independently approved qualification and live serving permission.
Remaining material review: inspect scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh, scripts/provider-release-swift.sh and .github/actions/provider-release-build to verify fail-closed release SDK 27.2/Swift 6.4.2 selection, environment/wrapper persistence across build and signing steps, actual linked-SDK identity for resumed artifacts, and cache compatibility across qualification/release modes. Their implementations are absent from the replay; this is an unresolved enforcement contract, not an observed missing control or proven cache-poisoning path.
